# Experiment code cleanup audit

**Question** Which files support the current paper and experiment workflows, and which files can be removed?

**Short answer** The audit identifies 12,078 concrete files to retain, nine conditional source-code retirement candidates, and 25 generated bytecode candidates.

- This is not a 100% deletion certificate.
  - The 1,204-file code inventory contains 664 files whose retention status remains unresolved.
  - Do not delete those files or treat the complement of the keep list as a delete list.
- No source, experiment data, paper files, branches or commits were changed or deleted.
  - Only audit reports were authored.
  - One agent ran 65 focused metric regression tests, which passed.
  - No negotiation experiments or paid judge calls were run.

## What was covered?

- Used 45 subagents in three waves of 15, as requested.
  - E01–E36 cover experiment and result-analysis families.
  - E37–E42 cover game generation, the protocol, model selection and metric methods.
  - E43–E45 cover tests, operational tools and cleanup checks.
- Each result family includes its game settings, model comparisons and reported subclaims.
  - A table with many coefficients is one analysis family, not a separate experiment for every coefficient.
- Parsed the current ICLR sources and mapped all 30 figures and 10 numbered tables to audit assignments.
  - Appendix prompt examples and method formulas are covered separately by E37–E42.
  - Figure and table numbers in the coverage file follow source order.
- Used the codex-search skill to locate prior work, including the requested September 5 figure-reconstruction session.
  - Agents then checked original history records, source code, saved configurations and raw outputs.
  - Prior summaries were leads, not sufficient proof of provenance.
- The current paper's 7,160-run subtotal comprises 1,500 primary runs, 500 Llama runs, 2,900 multiagent runs, 100 team runs and 2,160 TTC runs.
  - The separate 25-run matched GPT-5.4 coalition replication is also covered.
  - Those 25 runs are outside the 7,160 subtotal.

## Which source files are cleanup candidates?

- The strongest candidates are seven generic Claude planning helpers, totaling 106,646 bytes.
  - They are separate from the experiment runtime's utility module.
  - Checked runtime imports, tests, tracked references, configured hooks and commands do not use them.
  - Their only Git commit is from July 2025, and their default output locations are absent.
  - Their contents are generic planning, checkpoint and verification tools, not negotiation experiment logic.
  - Manual or external CLI use remains unverified, so retirement is conditional on no longer needing those tools.

| Exact path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/utils/context_analyzer.py` | Generic context/file selection |
| `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/utils/session_manager.py` | Claude checkpoint management |
| `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/utils/spec_validator.py` | Markdown requirement checks and test skeletons |
| `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/utils/task_manager.py` | Generic task-board management |
| `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/utils/todo_manager.py` | Generic to-do conversion |
| `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/utils/verification_framework.py` | Generic application verification examples |
| `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/utils/verification_metrics.py` | Generic verification and token-cost statistics |

- Two TTC preview renderers are separate, optional candidates totaling 9,659 bytes.
  - `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/scripts/plot_ttc_average_target_utility.py` retains an incomplete eight-seed Claude annotation.
  - `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/scripts/plot_ttc_five_seed_portrait.py` renders an older five-seed preview.
  - Neither is a verified input to the current paper results or retained code paths checked here.
  - They are plot code, so treat their retirement separately from the requested experiment-runtime cleanup.
  - Keep them if the historical previews remain useful.
- The 25 bytecode candidates total 766,944 bytes.
  - Each has an existing source counterpart and a matching interpreter magic number, source timestamp and source size.
  - Removing those exact generated files does not remove test logic.
  - This is a small cache cleanup, not a substantial simplification of the experiment code.

## What looks disposable but must stay?

- Dated review and reconstruction folders contain active code and inputs.
  - The current TTC figure uses `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/lh_review_20260829/07_halfwidth_footnote/make_candidate.py`.
  - The revised rounds result uses `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/analysis/rounds_all_runs_20260907/render.py`.
  - The baseline-label renderer reads earlier figure-reconstruction scripts and CSVs.
  - Current team and fairness figures also depend on dated review code.
- Older TTC analysis names hide current imports.
  - `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/scripts/analyze_ttc_three_seeds.py` and `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/scripts/analyze_ttc_five_seeds.py` remain dependencies of the ten-seed analysis.
- An apparent documentation file affects runtime behavior.
  - `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/docs/guides/chatbot_arena_elo_scores_2026_03_31_smooth_33_models.md` supplies model metadata and context limits.
- Excluded, failed and replaced runs can be required inputs or provenance.
  - A current homogeneous loader reads all 325 original runs before excluding 25 Haiku runs.
  - The revised rounds plot includes failed agreements.
  - TTC output-cap recoveries and in-place replacements require their saved configurations and attempt records.
- The old cleanup archive contains required replacement records.
  - The root audit recovered 27 exact manifest, configuration and launch files inside `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/experiments/results/TO_DELETE_20260809`.
  - These recover part of the primary Game 2 and Game 3 launch history that agents could not find at its original location.
  - [Recovered archive report](/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/docs/analysis/paper_code_audit_20260907/root_recovered_archives.md) explains the selection.
- Tests, viewers and configured hooks support workflows beyond paper generation.
  - TTC tests read ignored saved experiment data.
  - The annotation-review UI has current tests and documentation.
  - `/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/.claude/worktrees/contract-negotiation` is a registered worktree, not a disposable duplicate.

## Why is a 100% keep/delete decision not supported?

- Current source does not always reproduce historical runs from the same seed and configuration.
  - Saved token limits differ from present generator defaults in some cohorts.
  - Preference generation and runtime code changed after initial execution.
  - Some historical manifests record dirty worktrees rather than an exact source snapshot.
- Similar analysis files can encode different definitions.
  - Main and appendix fairness use different solver or normalization paths.
  - The current main behavior figure includes a 15-transcript repair that the per-tag table omits.
  - Discounted welfare ratios differ from a similarly named undiscounted CSV column.
  - Those files cannot be declared interchangeable duplicates.
- Existing cleanup manifests are stale.
  - The old paper-data manifest has 7,143 rows and does not describe the current 7,160-run subtotal.
  - It is still read by some current loaders, so retain it as an input while avoiding its use as a deletion allowlist.
  - Earlier blanket deletion recommendations for Slurm logs, archives and retained analysis are unsafe for the current paper.
- The filename inventory covers `.py`, `.sh`, `.sbatch`, `.toml`, `.yml` and `.yaml` files, including ignored directories.
  - It excludes virtual environments, Git internals, package caches and symlinked directories.
  - It is not an inventory of every JSON configuration, notebook, extensionless script or external dependency.
- The 664 unresolved code paths were not all given a complete semantic review.
  - Many are old analysis, reconstruction, launch or paper-support variants.
  - Some were inspected but still have an unclear optional workflow or historical role.
  - Their unresolved status is not evidence of non-use.
- The root static-import check added six needed files missed by the individual inventories.
  - It checked 284 seed Python files and a 290-file import closure.
  - It does not prove all dynamic imports, subprocess calls or manually invoked commands are covered.
  - [Import cross-check](/scratch/gpfs/DANQIC/jz4391/bargain/docs/analysis/paper_code_audit_20260907/root_import_closure.md) records the scope.

## Recommended decision

- Keep the verified dependencies, selected data, provenance and unresolved files.
- If you no longer use the seven generic Claude helpers, they are the clearest source-code retirement candidates.
- Treat the two old plotting frontends as a separate optional decision.
- Do not begin a broad deletion from old manifests, directory names or missing paper references.
- The paper-result coverage audit is complete, but a complete binary classification of every codebase file is not.
